page.layout: One page of text, full width, with a centred section heading and an italic subheading above the running text. A catchword stands at the bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Numerant Copti per literas ut reliqui Orientales, & hos numeros ut & literarum fere omnium nomina & figuras à Graecis Ptolomaeorum tempore mutati sunt, addunt virgulam supra literam ut Arabes; in millenariis vero infra, habent & alias numerorum notas sibi proprias.
main_text.head: SECT. II.
main_text.p: Vida, seu v consona, effertur ut b.
Hida, similis est Graecae literae (η) & sonat ut I declinans ad E, at cum habet accentum sonat ut I clarum.
Ni in fine dictionis formam mutat, & extenditur infra lineam, ut Hebraicum mun in fine ן[?].
He, aliquando ut I, & (y) & post Alpha ut (v) vocalis.
Phi, aliquando P. declinans ad B.
Chi, absque aspiratione ut χ Graecum à Gallis.
Scei, ut Sc. ut ש[?] Hebræum & ش Arab-cum.

page.notes: The Greek eta, theta and chi are read from the printed forms; "(y)" is printed in Latin letters as shown. The Hebrew final letter after "mun in fine" (printed as a hooked stroke below the line) is uncertain: read as ן[?]. The glyph after "Ebsi, ut" is unclear and marked illegible. The Hebrew letter after "Sc. ut" is uncertain (ש[?]). The Arabic letter after "&" is read as ش from a small, unclear printed form. The large initial V of "Vida" is joined to the word as printed. Bottom right: the catchword "Chei," is printed, and the page number is "(110)" in old numerals.
